para.text: : in 3D text mode the text is constructed as a 3D objects that follow the rules of perspective.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:24px left ;
para.text: The text is constructed in memory on a dummy canvas, and the pixels of the characters (not the background) are copied unto the screen. This is a pixel-by-pixel operation that takes some time. Best results are obtained with larger fonts or high-res applications.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:24px left ;
para.text: The size of the text is correct at the centre of the frame. For locations in front of that the text appears larger. Therefore the dummy text is created in a larger font to get sufficient pixels (depending on viewing position). This works well for all but the most severe viewing conditions. The change of font size may be noticed, notably when the font switches from a one-pixel-linewidth to a two-pixels-linewidth. Note that this only works fine for True-Type fonts (the default font Arial is OK). It is possible to fine-tune the size of the dummy text by

text.style: font-family:'Times New Roman'; font-size:12pt; text-decoration:underline; color:#000080;

para.text: ; this is a scaling factor, a value of 1 (or 0) does not alter the setting. A too small size will produce 'open' characters, a too large size consumes plotting time; in most cases the default settings however will do.
